answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, networks can enforce latency-based proofs using beacon hubs, such as a telemetry wharf grounded in basalt bedrock. Agents must complete timed signature exchanges across a radial lotus topology, forcing an attacker to deploy distinct physical transceivers and incur geographic hardware costs per identity. However, network jitter can trigger false rejections, and adversaries can still tunnel verification traffic through fast proxy relays.
